titleEn: Don't Know It? Don't Eat It!

pages.text: "Taro, look! So shiny!" Round berries filled a bush by the village road. Sharp-eared deer Mumu stretched their neck to see.
"They look like sweets. I'll try just one!" Mumu picked a berry. It rolled smoothly around their palm.
Mumu lifted it toward their mouth. Taro's quick hand caught their wrist. "What kind of berry is that?"
"I don't know. It just... looks tasty." "Don't eat things you don't know." Taro shook his head. They gently set the berry on a leaf.
They ran to Mumu's porch. "Grandma, there are shiny berries on that bush. Can we eat them?" "Those are for birds. They'll hurt our tummies."

Grandma washed Mumu's hands in the basin first, then put bananas on a leaf plate. "Eat things you know." Taro held up fingers one by one. "One, don't touch! Two, don't put it in your mouth! Three, ask a grown-up!"
Mumu called, "Don't Know It? Don't Eat It!" Then their ears turned to rustling in the bush. A bird was picking and eating a berry.
On the way back, an unfamiliar mushroom stood up from the ground. Mumu stopped their reaching hand. "Taro, what's that? I haven't touched it!"
Now Mumu stopped their hands at unknown things. "One, don't touch! Two, don't put it in my mouth! Three, ask!" Mumu reminded Taro, too. "Don't Know It? Don't Eat It!"
Grandma sat Mumu snugly on her lap. "Thank you for waiting and asking." However tasty it looked, an unknown thing stayed out of the mouth. Mumu munched a banana. "Don't Know It? Don't Eat It!"
